//: Who had a car on a day, read off the assignment log. The rule exists
twice: driver_on() in supabase/migrations/0080_company.sql, which the
daily push run and the console ask, and AssignmentResolution.driverOn in
exports and the reimbursements read. One is SQL and the other Dart, so
neither can call the other, and an export that named a different driver
from the push would be found by the driver, not by a test. Both suites
test_rls/rls_test.dart, the 'company: roles, assignments and drivers' group
Every id is a label. The RLS suite maps users and vehicles onto the rows
it created; the Dart test uses them as they are. A window is inclusive at
both ends and an open one has no end; a day nobody had the car resolves
to null, which every reader says rather than guesses.

cases.name: the last day of a window is still that driver's
the day after a handover is the next driver's
an open window has no end
before the first assignment there is nobody
a one-day assignment covers its day
a car never assigned belongs to nobody
